title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from p.23 and this page (the last of the folder; it breaks off mid-sentence). Grothendieck is setting up an axiomatic framework for 'tame' (modérée) topological shapes. There is a set S of 'arcs' (closed segments) in a space. For an arc I and points u, v on I, I_{u,v} is the sub-arc between them, ∂I is the pair of endpoints, and bor_u(I) is (apparently) the germ or branch ('bout'/'bord') of I at u. The axioms are labelled F_1, F_2, ...

Axiom F_6, as used on p.23: if two arcs issuing from x have the same germ at x, both are initial sub-arcs of a single arc K with x ∈ ∂K. So two arcs with the same endpoints and the same germ at one endpoint coincide.

The proposition under proof. Let I ≠ J be arcs with ∂I = ∂J = {x, y}. Then:
(1) bor_x I ≠ bor_x J. This was done on p.23: otherwise F_6 gives I = J, hence bor_y I = bor_y J, which is absurd.
(2) I ∩ J = {x, y}.

Proof of (2), begun at the end of p.23 and continued here. Suppose t ∈ I ∩ J with t ∉ {x, y}. Then t lies in the interior of both I and J. Consider the sub-arcs I_{x,t} and J_{x,t}.
- Their germs at x equal bor_x I and bor_x J; these are the two equalities written under the first line.
- So bor_x I_{x,t} ≠ bor_x J_{x,t}, and the two sub-arcs are distinct.
- They have the same endpoints {x, t}. Applying (1) to them gives bor_t I_{x,t} ≠ bor_t J_{x,t}.
- 'Donc en vertu de l'axiome des pts singuliers (F_5) on aurait bor_t ...' The page stops here.

The intended conclusion is presumably this. At t, I contributes two germs and J two germs, and the J_{x,t}-germ differs from the I_{x,t}-germ. The singular-points axiom says a non-singular point has exactly two branches, or that singular points are finite and isolated. So t would have to be a singular point. Either this is ruled out directly, or one perturbs t in the (then infinite or non-discrete) intersection I ∩ J to reach a regular point, which gives a contradiction.

The purpose is a basic lemma of a 'graph-like' 1-dimensional tame topology: two distinct arcs with common endpoints meet only at those endpoints, so they bound a 'bigon' or Jordan curve. This is a building block towards the combinatorial/tame description of surfaces and curves in the 'géométrie des formes' program.
errors: The argument is unfinished: the page ends at 'on aurait bor_t', so how the singular-points axiom yields a contradiction is not written. If I∩J minus the endpoints could consist only of singular points, an extra finiteness argument would be needed. This is presumably supplied by the axiom, but it is not visible here.
Step (1) is applied to I_{x,t}, J_{x,t} implicitly. That is legitimate, since they are distinct arcs with the same endpoints, but it relies on F_6 being stated for arbitrary pairs of arcs.

ideas.what: Axiomatic system (F_1..F_n) for a family of arcs with germs 'bor_x' at points, including an axiom of finitely many singular points and an 'analytic-continuation' axiom F_6 (same germ implies sub-arcs of a common arc)
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame (o-minimal-like) 1-dimensional topology; topological graphs / ribbon-graph style structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology program: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86)
ideas.where_published: The general 'topologie modérée' program is in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this specific axiom list is not known to be published

ideas.what: Lemma: two distinct arcs with the same endpoints have distinct germs at each endpoint and meet only at the endpoints
ideas.modern_name: Elementary bigon / Jordan-arc lemma in a tame category

missed.claim: The page is the abrupt end of a 1986 attempt to found 'géométrie des formes (topologiques)' on an explicit list of axioms (F_1..F_6, including a singular-points axiom) for arcs and their germs. It is a concrete, unpublished axiomatisation of the tame topology announced in the Esquisse, and the lemma being proved is left incomplete.
missed.quote: donc en vertu de l'axiome des pts singuliers (F_5) on aurait bor_t
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing Grothendieck's axioms with o-minimal structures, or with combinatorial models of surfaces (dessins, ribbon graphs), could show whether he aimed at a purely combinatorial-topological foundation distinct from o-minimality. This page alone is too fragmentary to establish that.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine step in an axiomatic development, cut off mid-sentence. It is mildly interesting as evidence of an explicit axiom list for tame shapes in 1986, but this page contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'donc en dehors[?] d'un ensemble[?] fini[?]' should read 'donc en vertu de l'axiome' (parallel to 'en vertu de l'axiome F_6' on p.23).
The crossed-out word is probably 'branches' or 'bandes', followed by 'pts singuliers (F_5)'; the axiom number looks like F_5.
The two '‖' annotations under line 1 indicate bor_x I_{x,t} = bor_x I and bor_x J_{x,t} = bor_x(J).
The page number at top is '29' (folder sheet 26).
